notes: The MKR Zero is not in the catalogue, so arduino-mkr-zero was added as a new part type.

Per the circuit image the MKR Zero is NOT plugged into the breadboard (despite the text); it connects to the breadboard via three jumper wires: red to VCC (3.3V), black to GND, orange to digital pin 7.

The image shows the 100nF capacitor and 4.7k resistor drawn off the breadboard, connected by short blue and yellow jumper wires to the DHT22 power/GND and power/data columns. I modelled this literally, with wire ends clipped to the component leads. Electrically it is the same as the manual's text: cap between power and GND, pull-up between power and data.
Exact breadboard columns (27-30, rows a-e) are estimated from the image; DHT22 pins are VCC, SDA, NC, GND left to right.

Validation fix: the battery's JST connector mates to the MKR Zero's BATT+/BATT- contacts. Those ports are now kind header-socket (was socket), so the battery leads join them as a compatible lead-into-socket pair.
The microSD card is inserted in the MKR Zero's slot (no ports on the catalogue microsd-card). I kept a joined edge only, with no electrical edge, since the card has no catalogued ports.
The USB cable used for programming is not part of the final circuit and is omitted. Resistor is listed as 4.75k in the parts list but 4.7k in the text and image; I used 4700.
